In [[cryptography]], '''Nimbus''' is a [[block cipher]] invented by [[Alexis Machado]] in 2000. It was submitted to the [[NESSIE]] project, but was not selected.

The algorithm uses a 128-bit key. It operates on blocks of 64 bits and consists of 5 rounds of
encryption. The round function is exceedingly simple. In each round the block is [[XOR]]ed with a subkey, the order of its bits is reversed, and then it is multiplied mod 2<sup>64</sup> by another subkey, which is forced to be odd.<ref>{{cite web
| url=https://www.cosic.esat.kuleuven.be/nessie/deliverables/D13.pdf
| title=Security Evaluation of NESSIE First Phase: 2.4.6 Nimbus
| first1=Sean
| last1=Murphy
| first2=Juliette
| last2=White
| date=2001-09-23
| page=22
| access-date=2018-09-13}}</ref>

Nimbus was broken by [[Vladimir Furman]]; he found a [[differential cryptanalysis|differential attack]] using only 256 chosen plaintexts.<ref>{{cite book
| author = [[Eli Biham]], Vladimir Furman
| title = Fast Software Encryption
| volume = 2355
| pages = 187–195
| date = 2000-11-29
| isbn = 978-3-540-45473-1
| doi = 10.1007/3-540-45473-X_16
| series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science
| chapter = Differential Cryptanalysis of Nimbus
}}</ref>
